Posterior subgroup probabilities

Source: R/group_analysis_probability.R
group_analysis_probability.Rd

Estimate the posterior probability that each patient belongs to each level of each subgroup variable, given the patient-level survival data and the published subgroup statistics.

Usage

group_analysis_probability(patient, summary)

Arguments

patient

Patient-level survival data, the output of group_data_patient().

summary

Summary subgroup statistics, the output of group_data_summary().

Value

A named list with one element per subgroup variable, in the order the subgroup variables first appear in summary$variable. Each element is a numeric matrix of the estimated posterior probabilities \(p_{ik}\) of that subgroup variable:

  • Rows correspond to patients, in the same order as the rows of patient.

  • Columns correspond to the levels of the subgroup variable. The column names are exactly the levels, in the same order as in summary.

  • Each row sums to 1.

Details

group_analysis_probability() computes the estimated posterior probabilities \(p_{ik}\) defined in the "Computation" section of vignette("model", package = "retrogroup"), separately for each subgroup variable. See that section for the formulas, including the error when any probability is numerically indistinguishable from zero.

The total number of patients of every subgroup variable in summary must equal the number of rows of patient. See the details of group_data_summary() for how to choose the counts. The standard_error column of summary is not used.

See also

Other analysis: group_analysis_summary()

Examples

  patient <- group_data_patient(
    group_example_patient(),
    arm = "arm",
    treatment = "Lev+5FU",
    time = "time",
    event = "event"
  )
  summary <- group_data_summary(
    group_example_summary(),
    variable = "variable",
    level = "level",
    patients = "patients",
    log_hazard_ratio = "log_hazard_ratio",
    standard_error = "standard_error"
  )
  probability <- group_analysis_probability(patient, summary)
  names(probability)
#> [1] "age"   "node4" "sex"  
  head(probability$age)
#>       under 60 60 or over
#> [1,] 0.5082235  0.4917765
#> [2,] 0.3946053  0.6053947
#> [3,] 0.4523425  0.5476575
#> [4,] 0.5422896  0.4577104
#> [5,] 0.4523425  0.5476575
#> [6,] 0.5055396  0.4944604
